<issue>Issue Title: [BUG] strands-agents 1.16.0 is incompatible with Pydantic > 2.11
Description:
### Checks
- [x] I have updated to the lastest minor and patch version of Strands
- [x] I have checked the documentation and this is not expected behavior
- [x] I have searched [./issues](./issues?q=) and there are no duplicates of my issue
### Strands Version
1.16.0
### Python Version
3.10.17
### Operating System
macOS 15.6.1
### Installation Method
pip
### Steps to Reproduce
https://github.com/strands-agents/sdk-python/pull/1089 introduced differences to how types are interpreted for ToolSpecs. In [nova-act](https://github.com/aws/nova-act), we have a few tools which are implemented via strands and which have typing.Literal argument types. See, specifically:
1. https://github.com/aws/nova-act/blob/9ea9851401bf5ee8223875f29fc17e3eb87d522f/src/nova_act/tools/browser/interface/browser.py#L75-L79
1. https://github.com/aws/nova-act/blob/9ea9851401bf5ee8223875f29fc17e3eb87d522f/src/nova_act/tools/browser/interface/types/click_types.py#L21
Following release of strands v1.16.0, users started seeing failures as follows:
```
pydantic.errors.PydanticUserError: `Agent_clickTool` is not fully defined;
you should define `ClickType`, then call `Agent_clickTool.model_rebuild()`.
```
We were able to resolve the issue by either fixing the strands version to <=1.14.0 or by setting pydantic to <=pydantic==2.11.10.
However, it would be better if Strands support newer Pydantic versions.
See: https://github.com/aws/nova-act/issues/79 for full information.
### Expected Behavior
`@tool` works when passing a `typing.Literal` type and having Pydantic 2.12.0 installed
### Actual Behavior
```
pydantic.errors.PydanticUserError: `Agent_clickTool` is not fully defined;
you should define `ClickType`, then call `Agent_clickTool.model_rebuild()`.
```

The collected context reveals a substantial part of the strands @tool decorator's internal mechanism embodied in the class FunctionToolMetadata. This class is responsible for:

1. Extracting function metadata including parameter names, types, descriptions, and return type from type hints and docstrings.
2. Creating Pydantic models for input validation by interpreting type annotations of the function's parameters.
3. Managing context parameters, signature validation, and docstring parsing.

Relationship to the bug:
- The issue arises from the strands tool decorator's processing of typing.Literal annotations in the function signature.
- The error "not fully defined; you should define `ClickType`, then call `model_rebuild()`" from Pydantic suggests the Pydantic model generated from the function signature is incomplete for some Literal types.
- Since the FunctionToolMetadata class is building this Pydantic input model from inspected function signature/type hints, if this class mishandles Literal types or does not rebuild models appropriately, it would cause this bug.
- The _create_input_model method (partially seen) is crucial as it builds the Pydantic model (self.input_model).
- Literal types, which Pydantic 2.12.0 might handle differently than older versions, require careful conversion into the Pydantic model schema.

Intended behavior:
- The @tool decorator's FunctionToolMetadata class should accurately handle all type annotations, including typing.Literal, converting them into fully defined Pydantic models compatible with Pydantic 2.12.0+.
